subject: chemistry
title: Chemical Bonding & Structure Adventure 2: VSEPR shapes and intermolecular forces
welcome_lead: Today you'll predict molecular shapes with VSEPR — and feel intermolecular forces.
meta_desc: Chemistry — VSEPR, molecular shapes, London dispersion, dipole-dipole, hydrogen bonding.
final_note: You learned VSEPR predicts shapes from electron pair repulsion (linear, bent, trigonal, tetrahedral), and IMFs (London, dipole-dipole, H-bond) determine bp/mp.

concepts.def: H bonded to F, O, N

walkthroughs.body_html:
Count electron domains around central atom; repulsion pushes them apart.

- 2 domains → linear 180° (CO₂)
- 3 → trigonal planar 120° (BF₃)
- 4 → tetrahedral 109.5° (CH₄)
- 4 with 1 lone pair → trigonal pyramidal 107° (NH₃)
- 4 with 2 lone pairs → bent 104.5° (H₂O)
- 5 → trigonal bipyramidal (PCl₅)
- 6 → octahedral (SF₆)

Lone pairs repel more than bond pairs.

Weakest to strongest:

- London dispersion — instantaneous dipoles; all molecules have them; stronger for larger Mr.
- Dipole-dipole — permanent dipoles attract (HCl, CO).
- Hydrogen bond — H attached to small electronegative F, O, N. Especially strong (~20-40 kJ/mol).

H₂O has bp 100°C — much higher than H₂S (-60°C) because H-bonds.

Ice less dense than water (open H-bond lattice) — floats!

DNA: A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds) hold the double helix.

Hybridisation: C in CH₄ is sp³; CH₂=CH₂ has sp²; CH≡CH has sp.

mcqs.q: What does an NMR chemical shift (δ, in ppm) actually measure?
options: Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
The position of a peak RELATIVE to TMS (tetramethylsilane, δ = 0), normalised by the spectrometer frequency.
Chemical shift is the absolute resonance frequency of the nucleus in Hz.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.

mcqs.q: What kind of bond forms between a ligand and a central metal ion in a complex?
options: Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
A dative (coordinate) covalent bond — the ligand donates a lone pair into an empty orbital on the metal.
The ligand forms an ionic bond with the metal because the metal is positively charged.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.

mcqs.q: Why is the hydration enthalpy of a small, highly charged ion very exothermic?
options: The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
Hydration enthalpy only depends on the size of the ion, not its charge.
Small/highly charged ions form strong ion-dipole attractions with water molecules, releasing a large amount of energy.
